text: What if your arms could move... without you telling them to?
Press the backs of your hands outward against the frame. Firmly, but don't force it.
And hold it for thirty seconds.
A neurologist described this in 1915. It's called the Kohnstamm phenomenon.
More than a hundred years later, scientists still don't fully agree on why it happens.
Right now, your shoulder muscles are working nonstop against the frame.
Hold an effort like that long enough, and even after you stop...
your muscles can keep contracting on their own for a few seconds.
Now let go. Step out of the doorway...
and let your arms go loose.
That's not you lifting them. That's your nervous system.
Responses vary. Some people feel only a little, or nothing at all.
